title: Site Leadership Coach: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: T4 plant and asset leadership: the site leadership team
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Draft learnings from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; validate them before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in_progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person, so this pack stays a draft until the investigation is completed and reviewed.

One source date conflicts: the gasket-history record quotes a change on 18/09/2019, while its own note and the narrative place the most recent change on 18-Sep-2020. The timeline keeps the 2020 date and leaves the 2019 entry out.

exclusions.reason: A reviewer voted to downgrade this finding; the Learnings Register leaves it out too.

bottom_line.text: The emergency plan gave the night shift no isolation criteria and no standing authority below the plant manager, so the decision to isolate travelled up a chain of phone calls while the cloud grew.
Isolation and detection were set up so that someone had to reach the release: valves closed only by hand at the valve, and detection that only displayed an alarm.

Workarounds became normal because nothing on site stopped them: a substitute seal used as regular practice, return to service at operating pressure only, and electrical fittings repaired only on breakdown.
Warnings were on record for years (repeat seal changes, pipe-wall loss, an unused change procedure), and none reached a leadership decision that changed the plant.

items.text: The maintenance and spares programme, one of the two largest hubs in the causal links, did not supply a specification for the 1986 meter's gasket or a reliability review of repeat failures. Supervision therefore could not act on the risk it saw, rules on the job were not enforced, and checklists were not followed at return to service. The pathway ends on a seal that was not to specification and was never tested to design pressure [FND-1A251687; FND-B440C1BF; FND-5919B328; EVD-8645; EVD-2894].

A culture that allowed unsafe work and applied risk management unevenly leads to gaps in the guidance supervisors gave and to routine deviations at the job. The findings read this as norms, not choices by one person: the substitute O-ring was 'regular practice', and the change procedure was not used after 2018. The pathway ends on changes to the plant that nobody reviewed [FND-8083ECAC; FND-B440C1BF; EVD-2986; EVD-8645].

Command and control resources and the timing of upgrades lead to equipment that was not set up for an emergency and to automation that was not provided. The isolation valves had no remote operation and the fire and gas system had no executive action. The pathway ends on an isolation that depended on people reaching the valve through the cloud [FND-044D1DEC; FND-6155A1C2; FND-9B406A83; EVD-3932].

items.text: Fitting a locally bought O-ring to a rectangular-slot flange was described as regular practice, repeated across three replacements in about 22 months, with no specification, quality check or recorded decision. Accepting a repaired pressure boundary after an operating-pressure soak had also become the modelled return-to-service practice [FND-B440C1BF; FND-A443D288; FND-71EE9734; EVD-8645; EVD-1494].

Breakdown repair was the accepted approach for flameproof fittings in the Zone 1 area, and twelve external-audit recommendations ran on extended dates with no record of the approval the procedure required. Both were visible in site records [FND-1280E788; FND-856F80CE; EVD-6916; EVD-6852].

The emergency structure ran as a serial chain: perimeter security, CCTV room, gas terminal control room, shift in-charge, overall shift in-charge, then plant leadership. No role below the plant manager held standing authority to close the isolation valve, so each step reported up rather than acted [FND-82761CC5; FND-A206DFD6; FND-4245FBF2; EVD-3932; EVD-6414].

items.decision: Give shift crews standing written authority to isolate and shut down on criteria written into the emergency plan
options: Shift in-charge isolates on defined criteria and reports afterwards
Control-room operator isolates on a confirmed release, shift in-charge confirms
items.trade_offs: Delegation removes the escalation delay but means accepting some isolations that later prove unnecessary, with lost production; the leadership team has to back crews who isolate in good faith.

items.name: Time to isolation in drills
items.measure: Time from a confirmed release to first isolation in each emergency drill
items.deterioration: A drill in which isolation waits for a call above the shift in-charge

items.decision: Needs corporate decision: fund remote operation of the emergency isolation valves for inventories that can form a large vapour cloud
options: Remote operation from the control room
Automatic closure on confirmed gas detection where justified
items.trade_offs: Remote operation is likely to need capital and a shutdown window; without it, isolation still depends on reaching the valve through the release.

items.name: Remotely operable isolation
items.measure: Share of emergency isolation valves on large inventories that can be closed from the control room
items.deterioration: No change over two quarters once funding is decided

items.decision: Needs corporate decision: approve fire and gas voting logic with automatic executive action for major-release areas
options: Automatic shutdown and protection on confirmed detection
Alarm with a timed operator action, backed by automatic action
items.trade_offs: Automatic action brings spurious-trip risk and engineering cost; display-only detection left the response to a manual chain.

items.name: Detection with executive action
items.measure: Share of major-release areas whose fire and gas detection triggers a defined executive action, proven in the last function test
items.deterioration: Any major-release area still display-only with no recorded decision

items.decision: Give one function ownership of pressure-part specifications and of approving any substitute part
options: Engineering function owns specifications; stores issue only against them
Maintenance function owns them with engineering approval of substitutes
items.trade_offs: One owner in engineering separates the person fitting the part from the person approving it, at the cost of an extra step for urgent repairs.

items.name: Parts issued against a specification
items.measure: Share of pressure-boundary seals issued from stores with a specification reference

items.decision: Treat return to service after pressure-boundary work as a hold point that operations accepts in writing against a test record
options: Hold point with a design-pressure test record
Hold point with an engineering-approved alternative test
items.trade_offs: A hold point adds time before restart; without it the meter went back online after an operating-pressure soak only.

items.name: Restarts with a test record
items.measure: Share of pressure-boundary jobs returned to service with a signed test record

items.decision: Fund replacement of old HPMV fittings in zoned areas with certified fittings, and move their maintenance from breakdown to planned inspection
options: Replace all fittings in the zoned areas in one programme
Inspect all now and replace on condition
items.trade_offs: Full replacement costs more at once; inspect-and-replace leaves old fittings in service longer but finds the worst first.

items.name: Hazardous-area fittings inspected
items.measure: Share of zoned-area light fittings with a recorded inspection in the planned interval
items.deterioration: Any fitting found with missing fasteners or an open enclosure

items.decision: Allow no extension of a safety recommendation without the documented approval the procedure requires, and review overdue items monthly
options: Monthly review by the leadership team
Quarterly review with escalation of any unapproved extension
items.trade_offs: A monthly review takes leadership time; the evidence shows extensions ran without the required approval.

items.name: Extensions with recorded approval
items.measure: Share of extended safety recommendations with the approval on file

items.text: Walk the metering area and the zoned lighting with the maintenance and electrical supervisors; ask to see the specification for one pressure seal and the inspection record for one flameproof fitting.
